analysis.investment_thesis: EIH (Oberoi Hotels) is a high-quality hospitality business with ~23% ROCE and virtually no debt, but at a market cap of INR 20,130 Cr against FY2025 EBIT of INR 1,028 Cr, the Magic Formula earnings yield is only ~5.1% — well below my 6% minimum threshold. Good business, wrong price.
key_strengths: Near debt-free balance sheet (D/E 0.05) with INR 378 Cr cash, giving financial flexibility for the ongoing expansion (CWIP up to INR 403 Cr)
Exceptional operating margins at 38.9% — the Oberoi brand commands genuine pricing power and operating leverage is evident as EBITDA grew from INR 48 Cr (FY2022) to INR 1,298 Cr (FY2025)
ROCE of 23.4% clears the Magic Formula 20%+ threshold, confirming a genuinely good business with above-cost-of-capital returns
key_risks: Overvaluation kills the trade: EV ~INR 20,017 Cr on EBIT of INR 1,028 Cr yields only 5.1% earnings yield — the Magic Formula demands >12% for a strong buy
Capex surge (INR 485 Cr in FY2025 vs. INR 138 Cr in FY2023) is crushing FCF — FCF fell to INR 346 Cr despite OCF of INR 825 Cr, and CWIP at INR 403 Cr signals more spend ahead
Revenue 9Y CAGR of only 5.7% exposes thin organic growth; the profitability recovery is largely post-COVID normalization, not structural acceleration
red_flags: Earnings yield of ~5.1% fails Magic Formula minimum of 6% — EV/EBIT multiple of ~19.5x is expensive for a hospitality operator
OCF positive only 3 of last 5 years; COVID destroyed two years of earnings entirely — cyclicality is a structural feature of this business
Promoter stake of 32.85% is low for a family-controlled luxury hotel group; FII interest at just 6.16% suggests limited global institutional conviction
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula on EIH: Enterprise Value = INR 20,130 Cr (market cap) + INR 265 Cr (debt) − INR 378 Cr (cash) ≈ INR 20,017 Cr. FY2025 EBIT = INR 1,028 Cr. Earnings Yield = 5.1% — this fails my threshold outright. On the quality side, ROCE of 23.4% and operating margins of 38.9% confirm this is a genuinely good business; the Oberoi brand earns real returns on capital. But the Magic Formula demands BOTH legs of the trade, and EIH only delivers one.

The FY2025 numbers look optically strong — net profit up 14% to INR 770 Cr, OCF at INR 825 Cr — but the capex acceleration (INR 485 Cr in FY2025, up 3.5x from FY2023) is compressing FCF to INR 346 Cr and will likely keep pressure on near-term earnings yield. The stock is priced for continued perfection at 26.5x P/E and 17.9x EV/EBITDA. I'd want to see this at half the current EV — around INR 8,000–9,000 Cr — for the earnings yield to reach 12%+ and make it a Magic Formula candidate. Until then, it's a HOLD for existing holders who believe in the long-cycle hospitality recovery story.
